name: Badagutittu Yakshagana (Northern Style)
keyElements: High-pitched Chande rhythms
Vibrant pirouettes and energetic jumps (Gudikattu)
Distinct bell-shaped turbans and large Kiritas
Emphasis on physical agility and dance steps

name: Tenkutittu Yakshagana (Southern Style)
keyElements: Kathakali-influenced facial makeup and rounded headgear (Kadlevale)
Continuous dizzying spins (Bramhari)
Rich theatrical dialogue and emotive acting
Dominant Chenda and Maddale syncopation

name: Talamaddale
keyElements: Seated impromptu intellectual debate without costumes or makeup
High literary Kannada and Tulu rhetoric
Profound philosophical interpretation of mythological characters
Musical anchoring by Bhagavatha and Maddale

name: Pili Vesha / Huli Vesha (Tiger Dance)
keyElements: Body painted head-to-toe with yellow, black, and white realistic tiger stripes
Fierce acrobatic backflips, rolling, and sheep-lifting teeth feats
Thunderous Tashe and Thaase beat accompaniment during Dasara and Krishna Janmashtami
musicalEnsemble: Tashe drums (steel cylindrical drums struck with cane sticks)
prominentGurus: Hereditary gymnasium (Garodi) troupes across Mangalore and Udupi

name: Togalu Gombeyata (Leather Puppet Theater)
keyElements: Translucent deerskin or goatskin puppets manipulated behind an illuminated white cloth screen
Enacts episodes from Ramayana and Mahabharata
Chanted prose and rhythm

name: Paddana Recitation
keyElements: Unaccompanied or Temere-backed oral epic ballad singing
Sung primarily by women during paddy transplanting or by male mediums during Daiva invocations
Contains linguistic memory of ancient Tulu syntax, flora, and feudal history
musicalEnsemble: Temere drum (optional) or rhythmic hand clapping
epistemicStatus: Documented living practice & Intangible cultural heritage
